subject: Intermittent customer egress failures — possible SNAT port exhaustion + MTU interplay
messages:
From: EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sporadic 502s to private deployment egress via colo transit

Marissa / team,

We started seeing intermittent 5xx responses for requests proxied to our on-prem Private deployment this morning. Symptoms: bursts of ~30s where requests either timeout or return 502, then clear. Happens across multiple customer instances that route egress through the coloc provider. Packet traces we collected show a flurry of retransmits and MSS-sized fragments.

We suspect something on the colo->customer edge (NAT/router) dropping large packets or rewriting ports incorrectly. Can you help investigate? Attaching a short tcpdump and a conntrack snapshot from the edge pair.

Attachments: tcpdump-edgecloud-aug09.pcap (stub), conntrack-snapshot-20270809.txt

Thanks,
Ana Morales
EdgeCloud Ops
ops@edgecloud.com

From: dev.patel@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sporadic 502s — initial findings (conntrack + SNAT)

Triage summary: I pulled the conntrack snapshot attached and matched it to the pcap timestamps. Notes below — raw extracts attached as conntrack-snapshot-20270809.txt.

Findings:
- Conntrack table shows many ephemeral TCP entries in TIME_WAIT and ESTABLISHED timestamp clusters around the reported windows.
- Several entries show repeated 5-tuple re-use with differing source ports but same SNAT IP; this is consistent with high outbound fanout from customer hosts and a limited SNAT port pool on the edge router.
- I saw SYN retransmits and a handful of DSACK/dup-acks in the pcap, and multiple records where a larger MTU segment is fragmented across the path (DF bit behavior inconsistent).

Hypothesis: Port exhaustion on the colo NAT + packet fragmentation (no MSS clamp) leads to retransmit storms which push flows into weird conntrack states; for some flows the router or SGs drop packets mid-handshake causing 502s.

Immediate asks (what I need to confirm quickly):
1) EdgeCloud/CoreColoc to confirm SNAT pool size and ephemeral port range — are we hitting the upper bound?
2) Check whether the edge NAT is doing port-preserving vs. port-randomization — port-preserving plus limited pool can exhaust faster.
3) Verify MSS clamp on the BGP/edge devices (we need a consistent MSS <= 1420 when traversing jumbo/non-jumbo links).
4) Security group/conntrack timeouts — any idle timeout < 60s could drop mid-retransmit.

Workarounds: increase SNAT port allocation or enable ephemeral port range expansion; enable MSS clamp on the edge; tune conntrack hash/size temporarily; add a short keepalive for long-lived flows.

I'll attach a short script to pull conntrack counts and iptables-nat counters if you want to run on site.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sporadic 502s — edge MTU + path validation results

Follow-up after hitting the edge devices with tcpdump and MTU probes (we ran ping -M do -s across the path):

Data points:
- PMTU probe failed at 1440 sized payloads intermittently; successful at 1400 consistently. Suggests an intermediate hop enforcing a smaller MTU or silently dropping fragments.
- CoreColoc confirmed that a transit segment to the customer's router is running with legacy jumbo frame handling; they have not enabled MSS clamp by default.
- Conntrack metrics (snapshots attached) show bucket growth and ∼30% of NAT table entries in the ephemeral range (suggesting heavy port churn).

Actionable remediation we coordinated with CoreColoc and EdgeCloud:
- CoreColoc: enable MSS clamp to 1400 on transit-facing interface (temporary, until we get full path MTU fixed).
- EdgeCloud: temporarily increase SNAT port range for the affected SNAT IPs and bump conntrack table sizing by 30%.
- Redwood runtime: add transient keepalive (10s) for streaming sessions that are sensitive to rehandshake during retransmits.

I recommend we monitor for 24–48 hours after these changes and collect pcap + conntrack snapshots during any recurrence window.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: ops@edgecloud.com, colocations-support@corecoloc.net
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sporadic 502s — remediation complete and monitoring plan

Update for EdgeCloud and CoreColoc — thanks for coordinating. Summary of the fix and next steps: 

What we changed (completed 11 Aug 2027 14:20 PDT):
- CoreColoc enabled MSS clamp to 1400 on the transit interface and confirmed via probe logs that 1440 no longer dropped.
- EdgeCloud expanded SNAT ephemeral port range by 50% and increased conntrack_max to accommodate the observed peak.
- Redwood runtime change: toggled 10s TCP keepalive for streaming endpoints in the affected customer config; will roll back if no further issues after 72h.

Monitoring plan:
- Collect conntrack + iptables-nat counters every 15 min for 72 hours (links: drive folder).
- Auto-alert if ephemeral port utilization > 75% or conntrack table > 80% for 5 consecutive intervals.
- If errors persist, next step is to route affected customers via alternate colo peering while we capture detailed pcap.

EdgeCloud / CoreColoc: please keep this ticket updated if you observe any regressions. We'll reconvene if we see any further 5xx windows.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Private Deployments Operations
Redwood Inference
